name: Segment head (boxes + mask coefficients + prototypes)

whatIsIt.eli5: Like the detect head, but it also colours in the exact shape of each thing, not just a box around it.
whatIsIt.simple: A Detect head plus two extras: a Proto branch that makes 32 general 'mask pictures' (prototypes) from the most detailed map, and a branch that predicts, for each object, 32 mixing numbers. Mixing the prototypes with those numbers gives each object's mask.
whatIsIt.engineer: YOLACT-style instance segmentation on top of Detect: cv4[i] predicts nm = 32 mask coefficients per anchor; Proto(P3) predicts nm prototype maps at stride 4; mask = σ(coef · protos) cropped to the box.

whyExists.eli5: Some jobs need the exact outline, for example to measure how much of the ground a weed covers.
whyExists.simple: Sharing one set of prototypes across all objects is much cheaper than drawing a full mask for each of 8,400 predictions.
whyExists.engineer: Linear combination of shared prototypes decouples mask quality from the number of instances; cost is one prototype net plus nm extra channels per anchor.

eli5: Make 32 blurry shape pictures for the whole image.
For each box, choose how much of each shape picture to use.
Mix them and cut out the box: that's the mask.
simple: The usual box and class branches run.
cv4 predicts 32 coefficients for every cell.
Proto: Conv 3×3 → 2× transposed conv (upsample) → Conv 3×3 → Conv 1×1 to 32 channels at 1/4 of the image size.
For each kept detection, mask = sigmoid(coefficients × prototypes), cut to its box.
engineer: YOLO26 uses Proto26: fuses all levels and adds a semantic-segmentation branch used only in training.

example.eli5: YOLOv8n makes 32 shape pictures of size 160×160.
example.simple: YOLOv8n-seg: mask coefficients 32 × 8,400 and prototypes 32 × 160 × 160 for a 640 image.
example.engineer: v8n-seg outputs: boxes [64,8400], scores [80,8400], mask_coefficient [32,8400], proto [32,160,160].

pytorch:
self.proto = Proto(ch[0], npr, nm)
self.cv4 = nn.ModuleList(nn.Sequential(Conv(x, c4, 3), Conv(c4, c4, 3), nn.Conv2d(c4, nm, 1)) for x in ch)
